encounters.cc: Progressive fatigue, weight loss, and increased urination with altered mental status

lines: Progressive fatigue, weight loss, and increased urination with altered mental status

The patient is an 11-year-old male with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosed six months prior, Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, and a history of warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia, who returns with acute worsening of hyperglycemic symptoms.
His mother reports that he has been drinking water constantly, even waking up multiple times during the night to obtain drinks or use the bathroom.
At school, his teacher noted that he has appeared more distracted and lethargic in class and has requested to use the restroom frequently.
His appetite has increased, but despite eating well, he has lost nearly 4 kg (9 lb) over the past 3 weeks.

His mother initially attributed the symptoms to a recent mild viral illness that circulated through his classroom, causing several students to miss school; he experienced low-grade fevers, nasal congestion, and fatigue but recovered fully within a few days.
Over the past several days, however, she has grown increasingly concerned as his energy levels have dropped further, and he has complained of stomach pain and headaches.
She also notes that his breath has developed a strange 'fruity' odor, and his clothes appear loose around his waist.
